FreeStyle Libre
in the UK. UK-registered digital health services supply these tools for at-home metabolic tracking and remote management.
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs)
Real-time data:
Tracks interstitial glucose levels 24/7 via a small sensor applied to the skin.
Alerts:
Sends automated warnings if blood sugar spikes or drops outside target ranges.
Clinical role:
Widely validated and recommended for managing diabetes and metabolic health.
National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov)
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG
Heart tracking:
Records electrical heart rhythms (ECG) and pulse data to spot irregularities.
PubMed Central (PMC) (.gov)
Consumer vs. Medical:
Most consumer smartwatches offer general wellness tracking rather than diagnostic-grade accuracy, though medical-grade options exist.
HealthManagement.org
Non-invasive claims warning:
Regulators advise caution, as non-invasive wrist-based blood glucose features on smartwatches lack clinical validation.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov)
Sleep Trackers & Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)
Sleep analysis:
Wearable rings and bands assess sleep stages, resting heart rate, and nighttime recovery.
RPM systems:
Connects home devices—like blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, and CGMs—directly to clinical dashboards for remote care oversight.
